terms.comment: Traupman’s phrase; not in Lewis & Short or the loci collections. It says “against my character” rather than “against what I think wise”.

evidence: Cic. Off. 1.110: invītā Minervā, id est adversante et repugnante nātūrā (Lewis & Short), s.v. invītus
terms.comment: Doing what one has no gift for, not acting against one’s judgment; for “against my will”, mē invītō.

sources: Lewis & Short: adversus · Lewis & Short: ingenium · Lewis & Short: invitus
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 101, checked against the searchable text and the page image (12 November 2026).
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
